text: In Middenheim they say that in the deep mines beneath the Fauschlag, workers heard scratching and squeaking in the solid rock at night.
Graf Boris Todbringer appears in public less and less. In the palace corridors people whisper of deepening apathy and black melancholy.
Word has come from Altdorf of new war taxes imposed by the Chancellor. The nobles of Middenland openly speak of treason.
Cultists of the Purple Hand and the Yellow Crown are making contact with bands of deserters and outlaws in the woods around Carroburg.
River barge traffic on the Reik has stalled; toll collectors in Kemperbad demand a triple war tariff under threat of confiscation.
In the merchant alleys shady figures in long cloaks have been seen buying up old plans of dwarf tunnels and sewers beneath the city.
A patrol of Road Wardens outside Altdorf deserted with full kit and black-powder weapons after their captain vanished with the entire payroll.
At 'The Leaping Hound' tavern someone is offering heavy gold rewards for word on mysterious deaths among physicians and scholars.
Wizards of the Celestial College in the capital warn of an ominous alignment of stars — foretelling bloody civil strife in the Reikland.
Smugglers along the River Delb report that dwarf holds in the Middle Mountains are shutting their gates against refugees from the lowlands.
On the road from Middenheim to Altdorf, columns of Middenland soldiers have been spotted marching south with a full siege train.
Bounty hunters are looking for a scar-faced man said to be stealing relics of Sigmar from roadside shrines.
Merchants from Marienburg talk of a steep new war levy — anyone who refuses to pay has both ship and cargo seized on the spot.
Talk spreads of eerie greenish lights over the Drakwald. Foresters call it witchfire, while scholars whisper of a warpstone storm.
Someone saw heralds in the Emperor's livery riding from village to village recruiting peasants with promises of 5 shillings a day and hot meals.
The local goldsmith actually fences stolen goods for a shadow guild. He keeps a double-locked stash beneath his workshop floorboards.
A forgotten smuggler tunnel runs beneath the city walls, dug back during the Great Plague.
A crew of river pirates wearing green kerchiefs prowls the river — striking only barges hauling gunpowder and firearms out of Nuln.
The watch is short-handed this week — after midnight the west gate is guarded by a single half-asleep old greybeard.
Someone saw a black-robed figure in the night dropping a suspicious pouch into the market square well.
The card-sharp in the corner loses on purpose — it is a trick. He watches who flashes gold coin and signals boys waiting by the gatehouse.
A traveller from Sylvania swears the dead march by night in the east. Nobody believes him, yet he flinches at every shadow.
The College of Alchemy in Altdorf has put up an astronomical sum for an undamaged mandrake root from deep inside the Shadow Wood.
At a Sigmarite abbey outside Ubersreik the monks bolted the doors from inside and toll the bells at midnight. Nobody knows what they saw.
One of the noble houses in the capital is quietly buying up huge stores of black powder and brimstone, paying gold without haggling.
